library(parallel)

mockJobData <- rename(mockJobData, time = X.U.FEFF.time)

job <- setClass("job", slots = representation(id = "numeric",
                                    time ="numeric",
                                    size ="numeric",)

queue1 <- list()
jobcount = 1

env <- simmer("Environment")
env

traj1 <- trajectory("Path 1") %>%
  append(queue1,assign(paste0("job", jobcount), new("job", id = jobcount,
                                                           time = get_attribute("arrivalMoment"),
                                                           size = get_attribute("size"),
   cutOff = get_attribute("cutOff")
                                                           ))) %>%
jobcount = jobcount + 1

traj2 <- trajectory("Path 2") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  x = 4

env %>%
  add_dataframe("job", traj1, mockJobData, mon = 2, batch =50,
              col_time = "time", time = "absolute",
              col_attributes = c("arrivalMoment", "size", "cutOff"))

env %>% run(25) %>%
  now()

env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
env %>% get_mon_resources()

So basically, I want to manipulate variables/objects/lists upon an arrival entering a trajectory. How can I do this?

Thanks in advance!

messages.body_plain:
I have a problem with an apple pack house that grades the apples based on diameter.  the diameter of the apples is normally distributed with mean around 59mm with a sd of ~5mm.  Once the diameter has been measured (using high speed cameras). the apples are sent to particular packing lanes to be put in tubes.  Multiple packing lanes are needed for the diameter ranges that are in the middle of the bell curve.  The shoulder sizes generally need only one.  We know the capacity of the packing lane and can therefore, a priori, work out how many lanes will be required for each size.  Hitherto only manual packing lanes were employed which all had the same packing rate.  We are now looking at introducing robotic packing lanes, in combination with the manual packing lanes, which have a much greater throughput.

When I simulated the packhouse previously with Simmer I used the branch command to deal with the different sized apples and the capacity of each resource (a particular lane(s) for each fruit size) to deal with multiple lanes.  Now I potentially have both robotic and manual packing lanes on the same sized fruit and from a resource point of view I wondered how I could deal with this? The fruit will be identical but the rate will be the much greater with the robots and the decision as to which lane to send it to will be generally be a function of the shortest queue.

I feel like I could use the Select command with a custom policy but I am unsure how to go about this.

Any help is greatly appreciated

Warm regards
Stuart

If you use an additional resource per machine with queue_size=0, then
you can have just one failure at a time and additional generated
failures for the same machine will be ignored instead of queued for
the repairman. Then you can just use set_capacity() to enable/disable
the spare machine as required.

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I try to rollback arrivals based on some conditions. I only want to let the arrival through that has an attribute (id) that is equal to the 'optimal' id (optIdRegion1). This optIdRegion1 is update globally using find_opt_id() once an arrival is released by a resource (pickOperatorRegion1). Then, once new arrivals arrive, I only want that the arrival with attribute 'id' equal to optIdRegion1 goes through the rollback and all other arrivals should rollback.

So basically, I want to select which arrival may seize the resource. For the other arrivals, I want them to wait upon pickOperatorRegion1 is released, and then I want to re-evaluate which one to have the resource seized.

Currently I used a rollback function (see below) but the problem is that arrivals are infinitely looping when timeout is 0 (i.e., no event occurs). It works when I set timeout to 0.1 let's say but the problem is that this 1) undesirable in terms of activity time and 2) in terms of computation time as all arrivals keep on looping.

So probably the use of a rollback is not the way to go for this particular problem. What would be the right way to model this situation where no FCFS principle is used?

env <- simmer("Environment")
env

pickingRegion1Trajectory <- trajectory("Picking Process") %>%
  seize("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1"))) %>%
  timeout_from_attribute("historicalPickingTime") %>%
  release("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  release("pickRegion1") %>%
  timeout(function() find_opt_id()) %>%
  set_capacity("pickRegion1", 1) %>%
  log_(function() paste("Capacity set to", get_capacity(env, "pickRegion1")))

region1QueueTraject <- trajectory("Arrivals looping in queue unless the arrival is the optimal arrival") %>%
  log_(function() paste("My id is", get_attribute(env, "id"), "and I am in region 1")) %>%
  timeout(0) %>%
  rollback(2, check= function() get_attribute(env, "id") != optIdRegion1) %>%

  seize("pickRegion1") %>%
  set_capacity("pickRegion1", 0) %>%
  timeout(function() remove_opt_from_regionqueu1()) %>%
  join(pickingRegion1Trajectory)

env %>%
  add_dataframe("job", queueVoedTrajectory, mockJobData, mon = 2, batch =50,
              col_time = "time", time = "absolute",
              col_attributes = c("arrivalMoment", "size", "cutOff", "historicalPickingTime", "historicalPackingTime", "transportationTime", "outboundLine"))
env %>%
add_resource("pickOperatorRegion1", nPickersRegion1, 0) %>%

add_resource("pickRegion1", 1)

env %>% run(50) %>%
  now()

env %>% get_mon_arrivals()
env %>% get_mon_resources()

However, I only want one signal to be sent at that particular moment in time as job24 only has to pass through the trajectory once. How can I make sure the signal is only sent once?

  timeout(function() remove_job_from_regionqueu1()) %>%

  timeout(function() decrease_picker_available_region1()) %>%
  timeout_from_attribute("historicalPickingTime") %>%
  timeout(function() find_opt_id_region1()) %>%
  timeout(function() increase_picker_available_region1()) %>%
  release("pickOperatorRegion1") %>%
  send(function() paste("Request for job with id", optIdRegion1)) %>%
  timeout(function() set_optIdRegion1_to_NULL()) %>%

env %>%
add_resource("pickOperatorRegion1", 3, 0)

env %>% run(700) %>%
  now()

Hi all,

Having an issue where seize does not work in a sub-trajectory after reneg in

Reproducible example:

simple.simmer <-simmer()

ia  <- trajectory()  %>%
  seize("resource", 1) %>%
  timeout(2) %>%
  release("resource", 1)

out1<-trajectory() %>%
  log_("i have reneged") %>%
  set_prioritization(values =  c(1,1,0), mod = "+") %>%
  log_("i have updated prioritization") %>%
  seize("resource",1,
        reject = trajectory(verbose = T) %>%
          log_("i have been kicked out for some reqason")) %>%
  log_("seized resource") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  release("resource", 1)

ib <- trajectory()  %>%
  log_("here i am") %>%
  renege_in(
    t = function(){  2 },
    out = out1
  ) %>%
  log_("waiting for resource") %>%
  seize("resource",1) %>%
  renege_abort() %>%
  log_("seized resource") %>%
  timeout(0.5) %>%
  release("resource", 1) %>%
log_("left ")

simple.simmer %>%
  add_resource("resource", capacity = 1,mon = T) %>%
  add_generator("r1", ia, distribution = at(1:10), mon=2,priority = 2) %>%
  add_generator("r2", ib, distribution = at(5), mon=2, priority = 1)

simple.simmer %>%
  run(until = 20)

get_queue_count( simple.simmer,"resource")

Output:

5: r20: here i am
5: r20: waiting for resource
7: r20: i have reneged
7: r20: i have updated prioritization

Expect that seize would be able to seize the resource in the sub trajectory.

Thanks in advance

Here I want to give each batch a name equal to `poolId` where each batch has a predetermined size based on the arrival attribute 'poolSize'. batch(function() get_attribute(env, "poolSize"),  permanent = TRUE, name = function() get_attribute(env, "poolId"), rule = NULL)

Above did not work so I tried to update some global variables poolIdGlobal and poolSizeGlobal once an arrival passed through the function get_pool_parameters() as follows:
timeout(function() get_pool_parameters()) %>%
batch(poolIdGlobal ,  permanent = TRUE, name =  poolIdGlobal , rule = NULL)
However, this did not work out as well.

What can be used to create the type of batches described above? That is, to determine if a new batch should be created (if there was no previous arrival with attribute 'poolId') or whether the current arrival should be added to a previously created batch with name 'poolId'.

just an identifier to be able to share the same batch in several
trajectories. The rule argument though can be used to dynamically
decide if an arrival joins a batch or continues.

Simultaneous events are tricky. There's a section in the JSS paper
discussing this. E.g., the send() activity always takes precedence,
because in most use cases this is the best option. On the other hand,
a timeout has the minimum priority if several events are scheduled at
the same time, so you could try adding a timeout(0) before the send()

Yeap, as I said, it's tricky. But in real world, simultaneous events
are quite rare. Using always continuous random distributions for
arrivals and service times minimizes these kind of problems.
